facts.claim: MDN defines a database as a storage system that collects organized data, making it easier to search, structure and extend.
The PostgreSQL manual describes PostgreSQL as an object-relational database management system (ORDBMS).
Docker's port publishing guide says that when a port is published with the localhost address 127.0.0.1, only the Docker host can access the published container port.
MDN says most of the code that supports a dynamic website must run on the server, and that creating it is known as server-side programming or sometimes back-end scripting.
MDN says browsers communicate with web servers using HTTP, sending a request, and web servers reply with an HTTP response message.
MDN says data pulled from a database is sent to the client to be displayed via code such as HTML and JavaScript.
Node.js describes itself as an asynchronous, event-driven JavaScript runtime.
Docker's port publishing guide gives the example -p 8080:80, which maps port 8080 on the Docker host to port 80 in the container.
MDN describes an API as a set of features and rules, a contract between the application offering it and other items, that enables interaction with a software program.
The PostgreSQL manual says a table in a relational database consists of rows and columns, and that each column has a data type that constrains the values it can hold.
MDN says that a request is made by calling fetch() with a URL, and that fetch() returns a Promise fulfilled with a Response object representing the server's response.
Docker's Compose networking guide says each service is discoverable by its service name, and that the web service can connect to the database at postgres://db:5432.
The PostgreSQL manual says the server listens on TCP port 5432 by default, and that listen_addresses defaults to localhost, allowing only local loopback connections.
Docker's port publishing guide says publishing container ports is insecure by default, because a published port becomes available to the outside world as well as to the Docker host.
MDN says the browser sends an HTTP GET request specifying the URL when a user navigates to a page.
MDN says large-scale websites use server-side code to dynamically display different data, generally pulled out of a database stored on a server.

Docker's secrets guide defines a secret as any piece of data, such as a password, certificate or API key, that shouldn't be transmitted over a network or stored unencrypted in a Dockerfile or in the application's source code.
Docker's Compose overview says Compose lets you manage services, networks and volumes in a single YAML configuration file, and start all the services with a single command.
Docker's Compose application model page says the default path for a Compose file is compose.yaml (preferred) or compose.yml, in the working directory.
The official PostgreSQL image page on Docker Hub says POSTGRES_PASSWORD is the only environment variable the image requires.
Docker's variable interpolation guide says the .env file should be placed at the root of the project directory, next to the compose.yaml file.
The docker compose up reference says --detach starts the containers in the background and leaves them running, and that --build builds images before starting containers.
The docker compose down reference says that by default the command removes containers and networks but not named volumes.
The docker compose logs reference says the command displays log output from services, and that -f (--follow) follows the log output.
The PostgreSQL manual says each column has a data type that constrains the values that can be stored in it.

The PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE page shows ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN for adding a column to an existing table, and says the new column is initially filled with its default value, or null if no DEFAULT clause is given.
The docker compose logs reference says the command displays log output from services, and that -f (--follow) keeps following the output.

Docker's secrets guide defines a secret as any piece of data, such as a password, certificate or API key, that shouldn't be transmitted over a network or stored unencrypted in a Dockerfile or in the application's source code.
Docker's volume guide says that a volume's data is persisted even if the container using it is removed, and that unused volumes can be removed with docker volume prune.

The official PostgreSQL image page on Docker Hub says that for PostgreSQL 18 and later the volume should target /var/lib/postgresql, and that for 17 and below it should target /var/lib/postgresql/data, because mounts at the other path will not persist data when the container is re-created.
GitHub's guide to ignoring files says a .gitignore file in the repository's root directory tells Git which files and directories to ignore when you make a commit.
The PostgreSQL manual says pg_dump writes its result to standard output, and that text files created by pg_dump are intended to be read by the psql program.
The PostgreSQL manual says that by default psql continues to execute after an SQL error, and that ON_ERROR_STOP can be set to change that.
The PostgreSQL pg_dump reference says that script dumps are plain-text files containing the SQL commands required to reconstruct the database, and that they are restored by feeding them to psql.
The docker compose down reference says the -v option also removes the named volumes declared in the Compose file, and anonymous volumes attached to containers.
Docker's volume rm reference says you cannot remove a volume that is in use by a container.
Docker's Compose overview says Compose manages services, networks and volumes in a single YAML configuration file, and starts all the services with a single command.
MDN says most of the code that supports a dynamic website must run on the server, and that data is generally pulled out of a database stored on a server.
